correctness.rationale: For the canonical increasing sine-circle lift with 0<K<1, the period-two equations sum and subtract to the reversible identities 2d=K cos(m)cos(d) and Omega-1/2=-K sin(m)sin(d)/(2 pi). Each midpoint has a unique d in [-K/2,K/2], proving the tongue is an interval. Eliminating m gives the compact one-dimensional width maximum; Q(d)=4d sec^2(d)(d sec^2(d)+tan(d)) is strictly increasing, so the sole critical point is the global maximizer. Rewriting 4 pi W/K^2 as max sin(2m)*sinc(2d) proves strict decrease in K (each maximizing m is interior), and uniform K->0 plus implicit expansion gives the coefficient 1 and terms -K^2/12+23K^4/1440. Fresh numerical implementation independently matches midpoint and critical-root computations at nine couplings to 1.43e-14; a finite numerical sample is not the all-K proof.
